title: Core
description: The starter types (the seven of the work, and system), task and decision (the shared set every pack may build on), the root links every link type extends, and the system tier.

types.title: Actor
types.description: Holds authority, owns work and is waited on: a person, a company, an agent. A starter type of the work: a pack's type may extend it, or extend nothing.

status.description: Where it stands: one of its statuses, an open one while it is unfinished. Kept in the item's row.

confidence.description: 0 to 1: how sure the author is that this is true. Kept in the item's row.

source.description: Where its facts came from: the source of the change that made it, or of its op. Kept in the item's row.

types.title: Aim
types.description: Why work exists: what work is for, such as a goal or a principle (a pack names its own). A starter type of the work: a pack's type may extend it, or extend nothing.

status.description: Where it stands: one of its statuses, an open one while it is unfinished. Kept in the item's row.

owner.description: Id of the person or agent responsible. Kept in the item's row.

confidence.description: 0 to 1: how sure the author is that this is true. Kept in the item's row.

source.description: Where its facts came from: the source of the change that made it, or of its op. Kept in the item's row.

types.title: Work
types.description: Open until finished; it blocks and is blocked: a task, a project, an issue. A starter type of the work: a pack's type may extend it, or extend nothing.

status.description: Where it stands: one of its statuses, an open one while it is unfinished. Kept in the item's row.

owner.description: Id of the person or agent responsible. Kept in the item's row.

confidence.description: 0 to 1: how sure the author is that this is true. Kept in the item's row.

source.description: Where its facts came from: the source of the change that made it, or of its op. Kept in the item's row.

seen_working.description: false when it is built, merged or done and nobody has yet seen it work where it is used; true once someone has. Left out, nothing is claimed either way.

to_see.description: With seen_working false: what would show it working, and where to look.

types.title: Question
types.description: Open until settled, by someone's word or by evidence: a decision, a hypothesis, an idea. A starter type of the work: a pack's type may extend it, or extend nothing.

status.description: Where it stands: one of its statuses, an open one while it is unfinished. Kept in the item's row.

owner.description: Id of the person or agent responsible. Kept in the item's row.

confidence.description: 0 to 1: how sure the author is that this is true. Kept in the item's row.

source.description: Where its facts came from: the source of the change that made it, or of its op. Kept in the item's row.

types.title: Record
types.description: Explains, and is replaced by a newer one: a note, a result, a procedure, a document. A starter type of the work: a pack's type may extend it, or extend nothing.

status.description: Where it stands: one of its statuses, an open one while it is unfinished. Kept in the item's row.

owner.description: Id of the person or agent responsible. Kept in the item's row.

confidence.description: 0 to 1: how sure the author is that this is true. Kept in the item's row.

source.description: Where its facts came from: the source of the change that made it, or of its op. Kept in the item's row.

wraps.description: The view or item it was made to give as a link: it is the link's own, and views leave it out.

types.title: Occurrence
types.description: Happens at a time, and can be a gate: an event, a meeting, a release. A starter type of the work: a pack's type may extend it, or extend nothing.

status.description: Where it stands: one of its statuses, an open one while it is unfinished. Kept in the item's row.

owner.description: Id of the person or agent responsible. Kept in the item's row.

confidence.description: 0 to 1: how sure the author is that this is true. Kept in the item's row.

source.description: Where its facts came from: the source of the change that made it, or of its op. Kept in the item's row.

types.title: Place
types.description: Exists somewhere, physical or not; work lives in it or uses it: a repository, a file, a machine, a licence. One that says exclusive is a resource: work that needs it claims it, one holder at a time when exclusive is true. A starter type of the work: a pack's type may extend it, or extend nothing.

exclusive.description: Said of a resource: true, only one holder at a time and everything else that needs it is blocked; false, any number. Left out, it is no resource and nothing holds it.

status.description: Where it stands: one of its statuses, an open one while it is unfinished. Kept in the item's row.

confidence.description: 0 to 1: how sure the author is that this is true. Kept in the item's row.

source.description: Where its facts came from: the source of the change that made it, or of its op. Kept in the item's row.

types.title: System
types.description: The app's own configuration, kept as items: views, styles, screens, runs, sources, notifications, automations. Views of the work leave it out unless asked: its types carry the kernel flag. Only the kernel's packs declare types of it.

status.description: Where it stands: one of its statuses, an open one while it is unfinished. Kept in the item's row.

source.description: Where its facts came from: the source of the change that made it, or of its op. Kept in the item's row.

types.title: Person
types.description: A human being.

role.description: What they do, in a few words.

types.title: Agent
types.description: A non-human actor with its own identity, such as an AI agent or an automation.

kind.description: What sort of agent, e.g. claude-code.

types.title: Task
types.description: A piece of work someone can do. A commitment is a task that involves who it is owed to.

recurrence.description: How often it repeats, in plain words or an RRULE.

tokens_estimated.description: How many tokens an agent expects this to take, one number: input and output together, not counting cached re-reads. Whoever plans it or picks it up says; it can be corrected.

tokens_used.description: Tokens spent on it so far, measured from the sessions that worked on it.

types.title: Decision
types.description: Something decided, or still open, with its reasoning. The title is the question.

options.description: The choices being weighed, as a list of short strings, e.g. ["Hosted API", "Local model"].

types.title: Finding
types.description: What an island has found, read in one line: the claim, its value, how sure, as of when. Marked published, it is what the island stands by, and only then may another island read it; the rest are its working findings. The title is the claim as a short sentence ("Peak load is 42 kW", not "Peak load"); the value is the fact, with its unit; confidence says how sure; as_of when it was true. The note says how it was found, three lines at most. An option is an alternative, a bug is a bug, working research stays research: none is a finding. Its readers read it (reads); a new value keeps the old one in the log.

value.description: The fact itself, never left out: 557, true, 2026-11-05, or a few words of text. A number takes its unit in unit; text says its own.

value_type.description: What sort of value it is: text, number, boolean or date. A measure is a number.

published.description: true: the island stands by it, and other islands may read it. Left out or false, it is a working finding, read on its own island only.

unit.description: What a number counts, read after it: s, kW, EUR, requests a minute.

as_of.description: When the value was true: the day it was found or measured.

types.title: View
types.description: A view kept on the map: a query (a filter, a walk and a limit, as query flat takes them) and how it is drawn, its layout with its settings, so a person opens it anywhere and it draws the same. About a project or item (an about link), it is a view of that thing; about nothing, the workspace's. where things sit on it is kept in the places stream under its id, apart from the map's. Named for the question it answers, its note's first line says what it shows; an agent reuses a view already there with the same name or query about the same items, rather than make it twice. Its life is its status: working (an agent's, about its task, until the owner keeps it; while what it is about is closed, it is retired with it), kept (only on the owner's word: Save in the app, or an agent told so, authority of human), retired. Home lists them; a document line holding its id draws it there; report show with its id opens one.

filter.description: What it finds: { find, only, not }, each a list of terms, as query flat's filter. find must hold something.

walk.description: From what the filter finds, along these links: { over: a list of link types or "all", steps }. Each is followed either way unless it ends in > (out along it) or < (in to it): a view of a project walks "part_of<", down to what is in it, since "part_of" climbs to its parent too and draws all of that.

time.description: A window each item is placed in, for a layout along a time axis: { from, to }, as query flat's time (dates, today, or days from today as -6d or 7d).

sessions.description: false leaves out the running sessions that come with what it finds (at most 8, those working on its items); left out, they come.

view.description: A view whose answer is items and links (such as usage), drawn in place of what a filter finds: then it needs no filter.

style.description: How it is drawn, held in the view: { shape, lit, style } (a built-in layout, what stays lit, a layout or style kept on the map by its id) and any style field that holds for this view alone, such as a grid's rows and labels. No code: that is a layout kept on the map. A shape here, or in the style it names, is drawn as it says: the code of a layout about what the view is of does not carry into it.

preset.description: The id of the pack's canvas this is the owner's version of.

place.description: Its order among the views of the item it is about: the lowest first.

steps.description: How the picture came to be, step by step, ending on the map as it is: a list of steps, each changing the one before from nothing. add and remove (lists of ids), titles and flag (by id: the title then, a word marked on it then; null takes it back), fields (by id, then by name), chapter (name, when, count: the chapter this step starts) and lines (by and text: what was said). The last step is the map as it is, whatever the steps say. What a step names is sent with the picture even when finished. The flow, grid, time and architecture layouts play them, with a step back, Play and a step on, opening on the map as it is on the canvas; a style's code is handed them as answer.steps. The list draws the map as it is.

types.title: Style
types.description: How the map looks: colours, type and sizes, and how a page reads. About nothing, the workspace's; on kinds or types (on), how every such item's page looks. What one view needs is not a style: a view holds its own layout and settings (its style field), so a style about a view draws nothing. How a view is drawn as code is not a style: that is a layout. A field left empty comes from the level below. The defaults are styles too: a pack ships them as presets, and one kept on the map with the preset's id (preset) is the owner's version of it, its fields over the preset's; retired, the preset is not used. Read only by the page that draws.

shape.description: The layout: map is the one that comes built in, used when the style has no code of its own; rails is the map with a walk through it: its items as stops in the view’s order, for a page read by scrolling. map: the whole graph made plane at once, islands and their ports with it (rings broken, trunks of one type and one way), given right angles with the fewest bends, then its distances relaxed keeping that shape. A shape no pack draws (one retired: list, flow, strips, rows, cola, grid, time, architecture, pages, planar) is drawn as map. Any other look is code of its own. map unless said.

lit.description: What stays lit as it opens.

published.description: pages: show what is published beside each draft. Left out, each draft alone.

order.description: pages: the order of its rows. reading: as a reader meets the site (the front page, the header by menu, then what each page points at in the order it does, the rest by title, the footer last); found: as the query finds them; title: by name. reading unless said.

undrawn.description: The link types drawn as no wire, as a list, e.g. ["about"]: the items are still drawn and still filtered by them. An empty list draws every link the layout draws.

link_colours.description: A colour for each link type, by its name, as hex colours: the flow draws each wire and tie in its own, and a type not named here takes one of link_hues, the same each time unless another type in the picture has it.

type_shapes.description: The outline each type is drawn in, by type: box, diamond, pill, sheet, cut (a box with cut corners), hexagon, flag, tab or ticket (a box with a notch in each end), e.g. {"question": "diamond"}. A type not named takes the outline of the nearest type it is a flavour of that is named, else a box.

held_up.description: Whether a step held up by an open step it depends on has its dot in the trouble colour (trouble), or is drawn as its phase alone, the order's wire saying the rest (none).

phase_marks.description: How a step's dot says where it stands, by phase (not_started, under_way, finished, ended, trouble, standing): hollow, half, full or none. A phase not named is hollow.

session_marks.description: How the flow draws a run's session state (waiting, your_move, blocked, working, quiet, idle, done), by state: { shape, hue, lit }. shape: disc, ring, half, square, diamond or triangle; hue: one of the theme's colours by name (you, blocked, session, warn, muted, done...); lit: drawn as what waits on you, and laid out first. A run whose state is named shows its line in place of its title.

link_hues.description: The colours a link type not named in link_colours takes, as hex colours: by its name, stepping past one another type in the same picture has. hues when not set.

key.description: Whether a picture's key is drawn: what each mark it uses means, as its layout says (the scene's key), always in sight on the canvas. shown unless said.

headless.description: The link types laid out from what they tie to, as a list, e.g. ["part_of"]: the whole stands over its part, and the head where its link points goes up into it.

ends.description: Which ends of a link type's wire carry an arrowhead, by type: end (where the link points), start (where it leaves) or both, e.g. {"link": "both"}. A type not named has its head at its end.

island_hues.description: The colours islands take, in the order a picture's answer names them, as hex colours: where a picture holds items of more than one island, the flow draws each as a region round what lives on it, its shore in its colour and its land a tint of it, and names it in the key. hues when not set.

place_hues.description: The colours places take, in order, as hex colours: the flow then draws no step for a place that holds parts (items of the place kind) in the picture, outlines each of its parts in its colour and names it in the key. Left out or empty, a place is a step tied to its parts.

layout.description: time: a calendar of days, hours running down (calendar), or each lane a row of bars across the days (bars, a Gantt chart). calendar unless said.

ranges.description: time: the numbers of days a reader can choose to draw of the view's window, each a choice over the picture beside All, e.g. [1, 3, 7]. A range as long as the window or longer is not offered.

hours.description: time, calendar: the hours of the day shown, as [from, to], e.g. [6, 22]. The whole day unless said.

open.description: list: how many levels are open as it first draws.

show.description: list: the columns each row has, as a list of: type, status, waits, sessions. status, waits and sessions unless said.

column.description: The least width of a box, in pixels.

text.description: The size of names, in pixels.

radius.description: How round corners are, in pixels.

gap.description: The room between things, in pixels.

colors.description: Colours by name, each a hex colour: sea, the ground behind the whole picture (the page's own); land, a box or panel on it; inner, the ground inside a box (on dark, the same as sea); line, edges and wires; text and muted, words; accent, what stands out on the ground, never the ground (the page's accent); blocked, you, session, done and warn, the marks for those states.

color_by.description: grid: the shown field each card is coloured by, e.g. kind.

rows.description: grid: what the rows are. Left empty, what the start holds. link:<kind>, the things those links lead to, e.g. link:could_fund: a thing is a card in each row its links lead to, with the link's words as its second line.

palette.description: grid: a hex colour for each value of color_by, e.g. {"grant": "#2e7d4f"}. A value not named takes one of the built-in colours.

labels.description: grid: what a lane or a value is called, e.g. {"set_up": "Set up"}. Not named, it is the value in words.

detail.description: grid: the shown field written on each card's second line, e.g. amount.

mark.description: grid: the shown date field marked on a card, with the field <name>_note before it when there is one, e.g. deadline.

sizes.description: Lengths a layout is laid out by, each by name: a number of pixels, or a length with its unit ("11ch", "68vh"). The stylesheet reads each as --ln-<name> (an underscore a dash), the layout’s code by name, e.g. flow_layer_gap. The house style names every one a built-in drawing uses.

numbers.description: Numbers a layout is drawn by that are not lengths, each by name: how faint what is not lit is (dim), how many make a checklist (flow_fold_at), how far a step of the wheel zooms. Read as --ln-<name> too.

hues.description: The colours things are told apart by, in order, as hex colours: a grid's values with no colour of their own in palette, and a calendar's streams.

start.description: The words of the quiet link at the foot of a page read with no login (a link’s, a published document’s, not a site’s own pages) that leads its reader to start a map of their own. Left empty, the page has none.

page.description: What an item's page shows, and how: picture (true to draw what it holds and is tied to above its note), notes (folded: a note opens on its first paragraph with each section a click away; open: every section open, each still folded with a click; whole: read through, every section open, as a document is), ties and history (open or closed as the page opens), head (invoice: a document read whole opens on its number, dates and what is due, from the fields its type shows). A preset on a kind or type says it for every such item.

theme.description: The page's colours, as light and dark, each a set of hex colours by name: bg, panel, line, text, muted, accent, ok, warn, bad, closed (each with a _soft), the kinds' g_*, edge, on_mark (words on a coloured mark), figure (behind a picture). Each of light and dark names colours, and derive names colours for both: a colour is a hex colour, the name of another, a mix of two (mix: [a, b], share of a) or one searched lighter or darker until it holds a contrast ratio on others (search, on, ratio); share and ratio may differ by scheme ({ light, dark }). The server works each out, so every page and agent reads finished colours. Read as --<name>, an underscore a dash. A pack that adds a colour gives it in its own style, as derived from these.

font.description: The typeface names are written in, as CSS font-family.

faces.description: The page's typefaces, each as CSS font-family: text (the work: items, notes, what is read and acted on), chart (the chart's names: groups and heads in spaced capitals, links in italic, the wordmark) and mono. Read as --face-<name>.

type.description: The text roles, each by name: face (one of faces), weight (400 or 600), style (italic), case (upper) and track (letter spacing, in em). The page and the layouts read each as --type-<role>-family, -weight, -style, -case and -track. The house style names region (groups, heads, places: the chart's spaced capitals), water (links and what flows between items: its italic) and wordmark.

notes.description: How a note reads, in the one dialect every page reads (Rule 11): callouts (for each tone a callout is written in, > [!NOTE], TIP, IMPORTANT, WARNING, CAUTION, the name of one of the page's colours, e.g. {"warning": "warn"}) and measure (the name of the page's length a note is read at, e.g. "measure"). A preset on a kind or type says it for every such item.

dots.description: What a part's dot says, where a layout reads it (architecture): field (the shown field it is coloured by, e.g. layer, in place of its health), colours (for each value, the name of one of the page's colours, e.g. {"kernel": "g_system"}) names (what each value is called in the key) and order (the values in the order the key gives them). Under the name of a look a story is drawn in (islands), the same again for that look: a field of status colours by the status, and the last value in order is done.

emblem.description: The mark at the top of the page, as a data URL of a PNG twice the size it is shown. A theme carries its own, drawn in its place's colours (scripts/emblems.ts).

icon.description: The map's icon where a browser's tab or a client listing this server shows one (/favicon.ico), as a data URL of a PNG; left out, the emblem.

page_css.description: How a published page looks, as CSS read after the page's own (ui/doc.css, ui/doc-lens.css): rules such as h2 { ... } or section:has(> .doc-lens.wide) > h2 { ... }, read only inside the published page. Checked when it is written as a layout’s stylesheet is (no url(), no @import, no quotes, backslashes, & or <), and refused with what is wrong. Taken from the workspace's style when a page is opened, so a page shows a change once it is opened again (or at once, opened with ?live, when it is published again). Written by an agent, it waits for the human unless the owner lets agents change layouts (agent_code).

on.description: The kinds or types whose pictures and pages it is for, as a list. Left empty, it is about what it is linked to by about, or the whole workspace.

preset.description: The id of the pack's style this is the owner's version of.

types.title: Layout
types.description: How a view is drawn, as code: a drawing kept on the map. It draws only where a view names it (its style field's style) or, about an item, on the pictures of that item; never as the workspace's. With code (code), it is a drawing of its own; with a pack drawing's id (preset) and modules, the owner's version of that drawing, its modules over the pack's; retired, the pack's drawing is not used. Its settings are the style fields it draws with unless the style or the view says otherwise. Written by an agent, its code waits for the human.

code.description: The layout itself, as a JavaScript module: export default function draw({ canvas, answer, style, theme, size, tree, three, on, open, tip, cursor, field, change }). It runs in the browser of whoever looks, in a worker inside a sandboxed frame: it has a canvas to draw on and no page, no network and no storage. Written by an agent, it waits for the human to approve it before it runs. canvas is an OffscreenCanvas (2D or WebGL); answer is what the query view answered; style is what it is drawn with: its settings, under the style and the view's own; theme is the page's colours by what each is for, as colors says (sea is the ground, so take accent for what must stand out on it; land, inner, line, text, muted, blocked, you, session, done, warn) and dark; size is { width, height, dpr }, kept current; tree() gives the answer as a tree ({ root, byId, me }, each thing with kids, up, depth and its counts all, work, blk, you, at); three() resolves to three.js; on(name, fn) hears pointerdown, pointermove, pointerup, pointerleave, wheel (each { x, y, button, buttons, deltaY, shift, ctrl }) and resize; open(id) opens an item's page; tip(text, x, y) shows words by the pointer (null hides them); cursor(name) sets the pointer; field(key, { x, y, width, height, value, placeholder, title }) puts a text field the page draws over the canvas (null takes it away), and on('field') hears { key, value, done }, never a key; change(ops, reason) asks the page to send ops as the person looking and resolves to { status, created, proposal, held } or { error }: it applies where it writes only the types in writes, and waits for that person otherwise; on('answer') hears the query answer again as the map changes (code that does not listen is started again). With code, shape is not used; a nearer style that names a shape and has no code (a view's own, one about the item, one named outright) clears it, so it draws only where nothing nearer says how.

writes.description: The types this layout's code may change by itself, as a list, e.g. ["local.ridges_setup"]: what its layout asks for (a preset saved, one deleted) the page sends as the person looking, and it applies where it writes only these types; anything else waits for that person (core's drawing_* rules). Written by an agent, it waits for the human, as code does.

modules.description: The owner's version of a layout a pack ships (with preset, the layout’s id): its modules by name, each a JavaScript module's text, standing in for the pack's module of that name. The layout runs as code does, in a worker inside a sandboxed frame, and answers with marks (SVG and HTML as data) the page checks before it draws them. Written by an agent, it waits for the human to approve it.

settings.description: The style fields it draws with, such as text or colors, as a style holds them: under the view's own, which say otherwise.

preset.description: The id of the pack's drawing this is the owner's version of (a layout in a pack's layouts).

types.title: Island
types.description: A cluster of work that speaks one pack's vocabulary and the shared set, below a project or across projects. On a map with islands on, every item but the kernel's own and actors lives on exactly one island (its field island), its type the island's pack's or of the shared set, and no link joins items on two islands: findings are how islands meet. The query term island <island> is what lives on it.

pack.description: The pack it speaks, by id (core for the shared set alone), fixed once the island is made.

pack_version.description: A version of its pack to try here, by the id of a pack item that is one (version_of): its types, rules and instructions are this island's while the rest of the map keeps the pack as it is. Unset, it runs the map's: unsetting it rolls the trial back.

types.title: Instruction
types.description: What agents are told, in its note, and where (for): as a style is how things look, an instruction is what an agent is asked to do. A pack ships them as presets; one kept on the map with the preset's id (preset) is the owner's version of it, its note and fields over the preset's; retired, the preset is not said. One kept about a repository is said only to sessions there, and over the workspace's of the same preset. A name in braces ({run}) is filled in by where it is said.

for.description: Where it is said, as a list: session_start (when a session begins), working_rules (the rules file a project is given), tool:<name> (the description of an agent's tool), guide:<name> (a guide an agent reads when it asks, with query name instructions and that for), file:<glob> (to a session about to read or change a file the glob names, as ui/draw.* or src/**/*.ts: what bites there and the way round it), server_restarted (to a session at its first prompt after the server restarted under it: how to reach the tools again), setup_behind (to a session whose folder's Archipelago files are older than the server's; {command} is the command that renews them).

order.description: Its place among what is said there: the lowest first.

preset.description: The id of the pack's instruction this is the owner's version of.

replaces.description: In a pack: the id of another pack's instruction this one is said in place of while its pack is on, worded in that pack's types. Kept on the map, it is not read: an owner's version names its preset.

types.title: Type
types.description: A type of item, kept on the map: as a style is how things look, a type is what an item is. A pack ships its types as presets; one kept here with the preset's id (preset) is the owner's version of it: its title and note over the preset's, its fields added to the preset's; retired, no new item is made of it, and those there are stay. One with a name and no preset is a type of this workspace's own, named local.<name>, extending a kind or a type of one.

preset.description: The id of the pack's type this is the owner's version of, e.g. task.

name.description: A type of this workspace's own: its id, local.<name>.

extends.description: A type of this workspace's own: the kind or type it is a flavour of, whose fields and statuses it takes.

fields.description: Fields added, by name, each as a type declares one, e.g. {"rate": {"type": "number"}}.

statuses.description: A type of this workspace's own: its statuses, {"open": [...], "closed": [...]}, when not its parent's.

deliverable.description: A type of this workspace's own: made for a reader or a customer, like a document; what it is part of names it under its title.

types.title: Link type
types.description: A type of link, kept on the map. A pack ships its link types as presets; one kept here with the preset's id (preset) is the owner's version of it: its title and note over the preset's; retired, no new link is made of it, and those there are stay. One with a name and no preset is a link type of this workspace's own, named local.<name>, a flavour of a link type it extends.

preset.description: The id of the pack's link type this is the owner's version of, e.g. depends_on.

name.description: A link type of this workspace's own: its id, local.<name>.

extends.description: A link type of this workspace's own: the link type it is a flavour of.

inverse.description: A link type of this workspace's own: how it reads from the other end.

from.description: A link type of this workspace's own: the types it may start from, as a list; any (*) unless said.

to.description: A link type of this workspace's own: the types it may point to, as a list; any (*) unless said.

types.title: Pack
types.description: A pack authored on the map: a way of working made of data alone, read beside the packs the server has. Its title is the pack's, its note what it is for, its name its id, and its manifest what it declares: types, links, rules, views (trees, screens, reasons for attention) and styles (looks, instructions, lenses), as a pack.json holds them (docs/packs.md). Every type, link type and rule it declares is named <name>.<what>. It runs no code: actions, handlers, layouts and reach are a server's packs' alone (a version of a server's pack may carry code of its own, code, run on its islands alone), and a rule in it only tightens, never keeps a stream or is lifted. It is checked whole when it is written, and it is off until the owner adds it (pack_set); the island rules judge it as any pack. Retired, it is taken out of the registry and its items turn dormant. An agent's edit of one waits for the owner.

name.description: The pack's id: lower case letters, digits and _, starting with a letter, and no pack's on this server (e.g. recipes).

version_of.description: The pack this is a version of, by id, to try on an island (its field pack_version) while the rest of the map keeps that pack as it is: never added as a pack of its own. It declares the same types and link types as that pack, by the same ids, and may change their fields, its rules and its instructions.

manifest.description: What it declares, as an object with the keys of a pack.json a pack on the map may hold: requires, types, links, rules, views and styles, e.g. {"types": [{"id": "recipes.dish", "title": "Dish", "description": "A dish we cook.", "extends": "record"}]}. query schema shows the types there are to extend.

code.description: A version's own code: files by path (handler.js, layouts/x.js...), each a text, standing in for its pack's files of those paths. Only a version of a server's pack may carry it, and it runs on the islands that run the version alone, under the same walls as the pack's own. An agent's word for it always waits for the owner.

types.title: Screen
types.description: A page the kernel draws as one column of pieces: a picture (a query in a style), rows from a pack's view, an action's form, an item's fields, a short note. On kinds or types (on), it is shown on the page of every such item; given a place in the nav (nav), it is a page of its own there; on Home (home), it is drawn there after the screens before it. A pack ships screens as presets; one kept on the map with the preset's id (preset) is the owner's version of it, and retired, the preset is not shown. Only a person changes a screen: an agent's change waits for them.

pieces.description: The column, in order: each {piece, ...what it needs}. picture: lens (a kept view's id, or a query { filter, walk, limit }, "{here}" in its ids, link terms or within the item the page is of), only (the types it draws of what that finds) and style (a style's id, or its fields, code aside); view: view (a pack's view of rows) and item (the input the item's id goes in); action: action (a pack's action); fields: fields (a list of the item's fields); note: text; count: section (a heading of the note), by (a field) and limits (for each of its values: max, low, high, split, emoji, link). Left empty, the preset's.

on.description: The kinds or types on whose page it is shown, as a list. Left empty, the preset's.

nav.description: Its place in the nav, after Home and Search: the lowest first. Left empty, it is not in the nav.

home.description: Drawn on Home (true) or taken off it (false). Left empty, the preset's: a pack's screen for Home is on it.

preset.description: The id of the pack's screen this is the owner's version of.

types.title: Source
types.description: The original input a fact came from: a file, an email, a commit, a conversation.

uri.description: A stable address: a file path, URL or message id.

types.title: Connection
types.description: An external tool, such as an MCP server. Status says whether it is reachable right now.

audit_log.description: Path to a JSON-lines log of tool calls, read by import_audit.

types.title: Run
types.description: One agent session or one execution of an automation.

name.description: The session's mark, never shown as a word: minted when it starts, none held by another open session, kept for its life. Its place in these values picks its hue among the style's, so two open sessions are told apart at a glance.

label.description: What the session's chat is called in its client (Claude Code's title, a bot's name for the chat): given at its start and whenever it is renamed, and its title.

stands.description: Where its place stood when it was last heard from, as its hook said it at each turn's end and at the end: a small flat object whose keys are the pack's whose place it is (a repository's: branch, head, worktree, unpushed, dirty).

ended_by.description: Why its client said it ended: clear, logout, exit, archived... Kept so a session started after a clear takes over its tab.

took_over.description: The run this session took over from in the same chat (after a clear): the owner's page gives it that session's tab.

branch.description: The git branch the session said it works on: a push to it is read against the session's task.

session_id.description: The id the surface gave the session.

packs.description: The packs active when the run started, as [{ id, version, manifest }], manifest the hash of its pack file: what lets a measure tell one version of the harness from another.

model.description: The model a launched run was started with, as its launcher was told it.

last_seen.description: Last time the session reported in.

stale_flagged.description: Set once the human has been told this session went quiet.

started_by.description: Who started the run, when it was not the owner: { kind: person, automation or webhook, id, name }. Such a run only proposes: its changes wait for the owner, whatever agents may do here.

tokens_used.description: Tokens the session has used so far, as its machine counted them.

active.description: When the session was at work: stretches from a turn's start to its end, as [from, to] date-times, oldest first.

busy.description: Set while a turn is under way: begun and not yet ended.

story.description: The story the session tells of its work, beat by beat (the tell tool).

cost_usd.description: What the run cost, in US dollars, where its surface says.

turns.description: How many turns the run took.

link.description: Where the run can be looked at, e.g. its page in GitHub Actions.

types.title: Notification
types.description: A message for the human, from an agent, an automation or the system.

types.title: Automation
types.description: Something done when a time comes or a query starts to match, about the item it serves: it lives on that item's island and is as visible as it. The kernel's clock says when it is due; the automations pack does it. Only fires while its status is enabled.

trigger.description: daily: a time of day. weekly: a time of day on the days named. Left out for one that fires on a query (on).

at.description: For trigger daily or weekly: the time as HH:MM, in the workspace's time zone.

days.description: For trigger weekly: the days of the week it fires on, as names ("monday") or numbers, 1 for Monday to 7 for Sunday.

on.description: Fires when a query starts to match, not at a time: { query: a flat filter as query name flat takes it ({ filter: { find, only, not }, walk, limit }), edge: first (it matches at all, once), each (each item that starts to match), first_per:<field> (once for each value of a field), or crosses:<n> with field (an item's value reaching n from under it) }. What already matches when it is set does not fire.

action.description: notify: tell the human, about what it is about. launch: start a headless session on a task.

message.description: For action notify: what the human is told; its name when left out.

last_run.description: The run the last launch started.

types.title: Shared document
types.description: A document another workspace on this server shares with this one. It stays in that workspace's map and is read from there each time, while it is shared: set it to accepted to read it here, declined or ended to stop. Only the document and the items it brings in are read. Where that workspace allows it, it can be published here, frozen as that workspace gives it.

share.description: The share it is read through, in that workspace.

path.description: Its address word once published here, as a document's: published only where the workspace that shares it allows it.

menu.description: Its place in the site's header, lowest first, as a document's.

links.title: owned by
links.description: Who is responsible for it: one person or agent, and a new link takes the place of the one before. Saying owner on an item makes this link; the row keeps its end as an index.

links.title: depends on
links.description: The source cannot finish until the target is closed. Drives the blockers view.

links.title: waits on
links.description: The source cannot move until this actor (a person, a company, an agent) has answered or acted. Say what is awaited in the relation's props.for, as what they are to do, in a few words, said to them: "Choose the pack's name", not "choosing the name". Drives the blockers view; remove the link once they have.

links.title: is part of
links.description: Hierarchy: a task in a project, a project in a larger one.

links.title: serves
links.description: Why the work exists: the goal, principle or tenet it is for.

links.title: is about
links.description: A note, file, decision or issue concerns the target.

links.title: needs
links.description: The work cannot run without this place; one that says exclusive (a resource) is claimed before use. Drives the blockers view.

links.title: holds
links.description: Current occupancy of a place that says exclusive (a resource). Created by claim, ended by release.

links.title: was started from
links.description: The session that started this one: sessions form a tree. Made by session_start with parent, or session_update with parent when a session learns it later; a run has one.

links.title: produced
links.description: The work led to this result, file or decision.

links.title: lives in
links.description: Where something is: work in a repository, a visit at a site.

links.title: bears on
links.description: Evidence on a question: a result, a test or a finding that helps settle it.

links.title: is linked to
links.description: The plain wire, drawn before its meaning is known: any link already says its two ends relate, so this one says nothing more. Nothing is a flavour of it; a link that means something is a flavour of the root it means.

links.title: uses
links.description: Relies on it to work, without waiting on it: a part that calls another, an app a team runs. Unlike depends on, it blocks nothing.

links.title: reads
links.description: Relies on a finding's value, from this island or another: the one link that crosses between islands. Its readers are who is told when the finding moves; when it was made, with the finding's history, says which value was read.

links.title: is working on
links.description: What a run or actor is doing right now.

rules.say: Code a version of a pack runs on its island is code that runs on the server: the owner allows it.
Code that runs in the browser of whoever looks is the human's to allow.
A drawing asked to change a {type}, which its layout does not say it writes: you look first.
A drawing asked to change code that runs, or what a drawing may write: you look first.
A drawing asked to make "{title}" public: you decide that.
What a screen shows, and where, is the human's to change.
Folding one style or layout into another can bring its code along: the human's to allow.
Making "{title}" one with another moves what is private to them, and their sign-ins and tokens: the owner's to allow.
What anyone can see is the human's to decide.
Its pack is gone, and its rules with it: a person looks at what is written to it.
The {pack} pack touched "{title}", a {type} it neither declares nor requires.
Settling "{title}" is the owner's: the agent proposes the answer, and they confirm it.
"{title}": to settle a question, say on whose authority (authority.of: "human" with where they said so, or "agent" for your own judgment).
Forgetting "{title}" is the owner's: it is for good, and cannot be undone.
"{title}" names a root pack: a root pack is the server's own code, changed only in a pull request the owner approves, never on a map.
A root pack is the server's own code: it is never taken out of a map.
The agent asked for a look before it takes effect.
This agent's token may only propose.
"{title}": a view or layout is kept only on the owner's word. Leave it working, or say where they said so (authority of human).
"{title}" is kept by the owner: an agent retires it only on their word (authority of human).
An agent's change waits for a person until the owner lets agents' changes apply.
Publishing is the owner’s here: they allow agents in Settings, under Agents. Ask them with publish_ask.
Taking a document down is the owner’s: ask them to unpublish it.
Agents may not download this workspace’s backups: the owner allows it in Settings, under Agents.
A run's story and spend now, two weeks of how they got there, kept half a year after the run ends.
What a session did, as raw events, for two weeks.
Who holds what now, a month of who held it, a claim kept three months after its release.
Who may read a notification, kept a month after it is read and three months unread.
When an automation last ran and what came of it, a week of it before.
The workspace's settings now, and a year of how they were.
When a token was last used and backups downloaded, a year of it.
A test's picture as it last ran.
The latest reading, one an hour after a day, one a day after a month.
What the reader pack counts on a public site (its counts): how many readers each source tag brought, per day. Counts only, every entry kept.
What was done that is no change to the map and is kept nowhere else: a push heard, a share made, a pack turned on, an act made outside. Every entry kept.
How often each thing a pack declares was used, per day: a view asked, an instruction said, a rule that held, refused or asked. Counts only, kept five weeks.
What a pack keeps, as it last kept it.
a pack kept as an item carries rules and words the owner may have added: changing one, or bringing one back, is theirs.
An automation acts later on the authority of the human who approved it: making, changing or bringing one back is theirs.

views.description: The query: a filter, a walk and a limit, answered as items and the links among them; the page names its parts Find, Only, Not, Walk and Limit. The filter is { find, only, not }, three lists of the same terms, each a set of items written as words: text <words> (the search read's own: words in any form in titles and notes, or as typed in a title, else titles nearly what was typed; the best match first, and matched says how many they found in all), type <t> (flavours included), held (what a change held for you would touch), moved (what reads a finding that moved since it was last changed or said still true), id <item>, in <item> (what is part of it, at any depth, not the item itself), related <item> (any link to it, either way), <link type> <item> ("tagged Urgent", "waits_on me": what has that link to it), <link type>< <item> (what it links to), owner me|<person>, kind <k>, and the words that can only be checked of what is found: done, blocked (depends on something open, waits on someone, or needs a resource not free, as attention says), status <s>, no owner, over estimate (tokens used over tokens estimated), changed since|before <7d|date>, made since|before <7d|date> (a since and a before together are a range, a date its day in the workspace's zone), by owner and by agent (on whose authority its status was last set). An item is an id or a name. find adds its sets to pick the seeds, and takes neither kind nor those words; only keeps the seeds in every set, types being one set; not takes its sets away from everything, an item named by id and what the walk reaches included, and the walk does not pass through what it takes away: kind system unless not is given. A filter whose find holds nothing is refused. The walk follows the link types named (over, or "all"), each the way it is written: "depends_on>" out along the link (what an item depends on), "depends_on<" in to it (what depends on the item), "depends_on" either way. A part links to what holds it, so from a project "part_of<" walks down (what is in it) and "part_of>" up (what it is in); "part_of" either way climbs to the parent and comes back down through all of it; for steps steps (1 when over is named; at most 6). The limit is the most items sent (500; at most 2000), seeds first, and cut says it cut. Each item is its head (id, kind, type, title, the start of its note (with notes "whole", the whole of it, for the first 100 sent, named in whole), visibility, status, open, owner, times) the fields its type marks shown (with fields true, every field its type declares that has a value, and its note whole, for every item sent, all named in whole: one read of a whole island, up to the limit), and why it is there: found (the sorts of term that found it: text, type, id, link, in) and terms (those terms, as the query says them) or step (the step of the walk that reached it); each link its id, type, from, to and props. With preview ({ part: find, only or not, terms, ids }), it answers only { preview }: for each term, at most 80, the items find would add it finds, or which of ids (what is drawn) only or not would leave out. With time ({ from, to }: dates, today, or days from today as -6d or 7d), a window it finds nothing more by: each item says where it falls in it (time, its spans; a session where it was at work) whose lane it is in (lane: the person who holds it, what no one holds the workspace owner's, each session its own) and what it counts toward (stream: the outermost item its work sits in; a session's spans each their own, with on_title), the lanes and streams in order (lanes, streams), for a layout along a time axis. Params: filter ({ find, only, not }), walk ({ over, steps }), limit, time, notes, fields.

The hubs within an item or a place (within, needed): open items in it that hold enough to need views of their own, largest first, each with how much it holds (inside), the size at which an item there counts as a hub (at) and how many views it has. An item is a hub when it holds at least its project's hub_at open things (12 when the project does not say; a project still being shaped sets it to 1, so that nearly everything in it is one). A hub with no views is work owed: give it its views with views (type lens) about it. Nothing is stored: this is read off the map each time.

Where a session stands on the map, and what there needs it: the open items the earlier sessions in this place worked on, one step along part_of either way, each with why it needs attention now, the strongest first. Reasons: corrected (a person changed or added it since an agent last touched it), waits_on, to_confirm, unsettled, left (begun, no session on it now), under_way, holding_up, blocked, moved, due, unseen (nobody has seen it working), open. Not a summary of the sessions: what their work reaches. What a session is handed as it starts. Params: run (the session asking: its folder is read from it), cwd, remote, limit (12); with none of run, cwd or remote, the whole workspace's recent sessions (what Home draws, as the flat term frontier).

actions.title: Capture
actions.description: Put something on the map: an item and its links, or a record of what happened.

actions.title: Assign
actions.description: Give work to someone, inside the map or outside it: an owner, a person waited on, a party asked to act.

actions.title: Report
actions.description: Say that something happened or is so: progress, a result, a payment, a check that it still holds. Also answers the owner with a view: show, with a kept view or an ad-hoc lens and style.

actions.title: Ask
actions.description: Put a question to someone and wait for the answer.

actions.title: Settle
actions.description: Close a question by someone's word or by evidence: a decision made, a hypothesis borne out.

actions.title: Revise
actions.description: Change, correct or undo what is on the map.
